verdicts.summary: The failure modes in this note are already in finding 0: the settle is only logged when it is refused or fails, a restart loses it, and the agent is told it succeeded. The branch condition and the activeRunId check line up with the live-caller check.

Finding 0 already covers the 24h fiber holding two streams, the duplicate fibers, and the silent no-op on timeout. A thread deletion during the wait makes waitForThread fail with RunNotFound, and ignoreCause swallows that, which is fine.
A pending deferred settle cannot be cancelled. An unsettle issued later in the same run is overridden when the run completes.
verdicts.scenario: 1) While its run is active, the agent calls t3_thread_organize settle on its own thread. A fiber is forked and the reply is {settlesWhenTurnEnds:true}. 2) Later in the same turn, the agent (or the user in the UI) issues thread.unsettle. It is accepted because unsettle has no active-run check, and settledOverride becomes 'active' (Orchestrator.ts:2787-2795). 3) The run completes. settleAfterRun dispatches thread.settle (ThreadManagementService.ts:760), which sets settledOverride='settled' and detaches the provider sessions (Orchestrator.ts:2769-2785, 3303).
verdicts.consequence: The thread settles even though the agent or user explicitly asked for it to stay active after the settle request. That intent is silently lost, and the provider sessions are detached.
